slides.1.title: 🌊 The Geographic Legend of the Mosel
slides.1.content: The Mosel region runs along the winding Mosel river for about 245 kilometres, from Perl (at the Germany–France–Luxembourg border) to Koblenz (where it joins the Rhine). The finest vineyards lie on the inside bends of the river, with slopes of 60–70° too steep for machinery and entirely worked by hand. The slate soil absorbs heat by day and releases it slowly at night, while the river reflects sunlight, allowing the grapes to ripen elegantly even at 50°N latitude.
slides.2.title: 🏆 Mosel's Top Vineyards (Grosse Lagen)
slides.2.items.0.text: Scharzhofberg (Wiltingen): regarded as one of Germany's greatest white wine vineyards
slides.2.items.1.text: Bernkasteler Doctor: the legendary medieval vineyard said to have healed an archbishop
slides.2.items.2.text: Wehlener Sonnenuhr (J.J. Prüm): famous sun-drenched vineyard marked by a sundial
slides.2.items.3.text: Ürziger Würzgarten: red sandstone 'spice garden' with distinctive pepper and mineral notes
slides.2.items.4.text: Erdener Treppchen: the 'staircase' vineyard, with breathtakingly steep terraced slopes
slides.3.right.items.2: Truly excels only in great vintages

slides.7.title: Quick Quiz
slides.7.questions.0.question: What is the special role of slate soils in the Mosel's wines?
slides.7.questions.0.options.1: Absorbs heat by day, releases it slowly at night, and reflects light
slides.7.questions.0.explanation: Slate (Schiefer) is the soul of the Mosel. It conducts heat well, soaks up the sun's energy by day and releases it slowly at night, keeping the vineyard warm; meanwhile its dark blue surfaces also reflect sunlight, helping the grapes ripen on these steep slopes.
slides.7.questions.1.question: Which is the most famous estate in the Scharzhofberg vineyard?
slides.7.questions.1.explanation: Egon Müller is the most famous producer in the Scharzhofberg vineyard, and his Scharzhofberger TBA is among the most expensive German wines in the world, having set record auction prices.
